tool_input.command: f=$(grep -rl "class Controller" node_modules/@guren/server/dist --include=*.d.ts | head -3); echo $f; grep -n "cookie\|Cookie\|back(\|redirect\|referer" -i $f | head -40

result:
The site now supports Japanese, and there's a language switcher in the header on every page, for guests and signed-in readers. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (9 tests, all passing) and `bunx guren check --i18n` all pass. The catalog check found 29 keys in both `lang/en` and `lang/ja`, and no page or component source contains 「記事」. I didn't start the app or try the switcher in a browser.

- **Remembering the pick:** `POST /locale` accepts `en` or `ja` and saves the choice in a `locale` cookie that lasts a year. Guren's built-in detection already reads that cookie before `Accept-Language`, so a saved pick beats the browser setting. With no pick, a Japanese browser gets Japanese; otherwise the site stays English.
- **Redirect back:** it sends the reader to the page in `Referer`, or `/` if there isn't one. Only the path is kept, never the host, so the route can't be used to redirect people to another site.
- **Invalid values:** anything else (`fr`, a missing field) is rejected by the same route-level check that rejects a bad post title. It returns a 422 and leaves the cookie as it was.

**Code changes:**
- **Route and validation:** `app/Http/Controllers/LocaleController.ts` and `app/Http/Validators/LocaleValidator.ts`, which also holds the one list of supported languages. The route is registered in `routes/web.ts`, and `src/app.ts` now takes its supported languages from that list.
- **Catalogs:** new `nav.json`, `posts.json`, `auth.json` and `locale.json` in both `lang/en/` and `lang/ja/`, plus a Japanese `messages.json` for the existing welcome message. All nine required keys have the Japanese values from your table.
- **Pages:** `resources/js/components/Layout.tsx` has the switcher and takes the header labels from the catalog. I also added a header link to `/` using `nav.home`. The four posts pages (list, post, new, edit) now read every label from the catalogs.
- **Generated files:** I re-ran codegen so the new keys and route are typed.
- **Tests:** `tests/LocaleController.test.ts` covers the English default, a Japanese browser, a saved pick beating the browser, the redirect with and without `Referer`, rejecting `fr`, and matching keys in the posts catalogs.

**English wording changes:**
- The header's "Write" link now reads "New post", because it shares the `posts.new` key with the new-post page heading.
- "Sign in" still reads "Sign in" in English, even though its key is `auth.login`.
